tagline: Small lakes and a message beneath the sea.
intro: Through the Chequamegon National Forest, the Great Divide Highway runs about 29 miles, crossing lakes, swamps and bogs on its way to Clam Lake on Highway 77. Clam Lake sits near the headwaters of the Chippewa Flowage, among smaller lakes known for musky fishing.
In 1995 the University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point brought a herd of 25 elk to Clam Lake, the start of their return to Wisconsin. The community itself counted 36 people in 2020.

moments.title: Foo Lake
moments.text: A four-acre lake in the national forest, fed by seepage from the surrounding swamp, with a muck bottom and, by the state's count, no sport fish.

moments.title: Clam Lake
moments.text: From 1985 to 2004, a Navy transmitter here sent extremely low frequency signals to deeply submerged submarines; it is now decommissioned.

sources.label: FHWA America's Byways, Great Divide Highway
